sections.h2: Where does an Anderson County deed get filed?
sections.html:
It gets filed at the Anderson County Clerk's counter, 100 S Main St, Lawrenceburg, KY 40342. Recording there is what makes a conveyance effective against later purchasers who had no notice and against the grantor's creditors (KRS 382.110(1)).

Lawrenceburg is both seat and sole city. A General Assembly act approved January 16, 1827 carved the county from parts of Franklin, Washington and Mercer. Sellers rarely go to the counter themselves, because the closing office carries the signed deed over, pays the clerk, and later returns the stamped original.

sections.h2: What is Anderson County like as a place to sell a home?
sections.html:
A mid-2025 estimate puts the population at 25,225, against 23,852 in 2020. The county touches seven others (Franklin, Woodford, Mercer, Washington, Nelson, Spencer and Shelby) and is part of the Frankfort micropolitan area. Workers average 30.4 minutes each way.

  • Typical owner-occupied house value, 2020 to 2024: $225,100.
  • Owner households: 77.6 percent of 9,653.
  • Housing units counted in July 2025: 10,652.
  • Middle monthly owner cost: $1,391 with a mortgage, $411 without.
  • Middle income per household: $74,488. Middle gross rent: $927 a month.

Owners far outnumber renters here.

About 202 square miles hold 25 named places, among them Alton, Glensboro, McBrayer and Stringtown. All of them are recorded in the same Lawrenceburg books, so a village name on a mailing address does not change where the deed goes. Population has risen about 5.6 percent since 2020.

sections.h2: What has to be written into the deed?
sections.html:
Under KRS 382.135 the clerk cannot accept a deed missing certain items. A short review before closing avoids a second trip.

  • Complete names and mailing addresses for grantor and grantee.
  • A statement of the whole consideration.
  • Where that year's tax bill should be sent, as an in-care-of address.
  • A notarized, sworn certificate signed for both sides confirming the price shown is everything paid. A gift deed has a certificate saying it is a gift, with an estimated fair cash value.

KRS 382.110 adds a title-source rule: the deed names the prior deed (office, book, page and date recorded), or explains how the seller acquired the land if it came by inheritance. A house that passed under a will, or with none, also requires an affidavit from the estate's personal representative, filed before closing the estate, naming each recipient and parcel and its value.

sections.h2: What will the clerk charge me?
sections.html:
The posted schedule took effect January 1, 2020. Each page past the fifth costs $3, and for mortgages the $3 starts after page thirty. A separate $4 state tax on each real property conveyance comes from KRS 142.010; the clerk collects and remits it. Check whether a quoted total includes it.

Minimum amounts posted by the Anderson County Clerk for frequent real estate filings (anderson.countyclerk.us)

A seller typically pays for a deed and perhaps a release, so the clerk's charges are a small slice of closing costs.

sections.h2: How does the state transfer tax work in Anderson County?
sections.html:
Under KRS 142.050 the seller pays $0.50 for each $500 declared in the deed, and a partial $500 counts as a whole one. The clerk does the math and keeps the deed until payment. Picture a $225,100 sale: 450 whole units plus a remainder make 451 units, so the tax is $225.50. This is an illustration only.

A gift, or a deed with token consideration, is valued at open-market price. Out of the tax, the clerk retains 5 percent and sends the rest to the county treasurer every quarter. These transfers are exempt:

  • Transfers by foreclosure, or by voluntary surrender under a mortgage.
  • Spouse to spouse, including former spouses dividing property in a divorce.
  • Parent and child, or grandparent and grandchild, for nominal money.
  • Deeds that only secure or free a debt, or correct an earlier deed.
  • Tax-sale conveyances and partitions.

The clerk's records page lists an Exempt Transfer Affidavit, Form 71A245, to claim an exemption.

sections.h2: What else can you do at the Anderson County Clerk's office?
sections.html:
The same counter that records deeds also renews vehicle registrations. The clerk's website asks online renewers for a title number, a plate number and a credit card, and it has a VIN lookup for the prior year's vehicle tax. Voter registration and election results sit in the elections department. A delinquent-tax lookup called DTax lets you check whether a parcel is on the unpaid list, though the site warns the clerk alone fixes the dollar amount owed on any bill when a sale happens.

Common forms are grouped as motor vehicle, legal records, elections and delinquent tax. Sellers mostly need the legal records set, which includes the Exempt Transfer Affidavit, a release of a real estate mortgage, a release of a vendor's lien and an affidavit of conversion to real estate.

sections.h2: How far back do Anderson County land records go?
sections.html:
Deeds and mortgages are indexed in CCLIX to 1966, and wills and marriages to 1797. Document images from January 2004 forward can mostly be pulled up online, while paper and microfilm reach into the 1700s.

Online access runs through eCCLIX, which requires an account from the vendor and charges for use. In the clerk's office anyone can read the same indexes and images without paying. DocAlert is a free email service: register a name, and each deed or mortgage recorded under it triggers a notice. Owners who live elsewhere or hold rentals can use it to catch a fraudulent filing early.

sections.h2: What if the property tax was never paid?
sections.html:
On April 15 the sheriff passes all unpaid bills to the clerk. The Sheriff's Office says payers there owe a 20 percent County Attorney fee and a 10 percent Clerk fee, plus interest of 1 percent monthly, on top of earlier penalties. Summer can bring a sale of the debt to a private buyer.

Under KRS 134.015(5) the lien can follow the land for up to eleven years regardless of owner, and a title agent will find it. Plan for the payoff to come out of the seller's net. Until April 15 the Sheriff's Office takes payment, at (502) 839-4021.

sections.h2: What is a sensible checklist before signing?
sections.html:
• Find your own deed and record its book and page.
  • Get this year's bill and any old balance from the Sheriff.
  • Ask the clerk about any recorded lien or lis pendens.
  • Write in the buyer's mailing address for the tax bill.
  • Prepare the exemption affidavit if one applies.

To sell as is, ask for a written cash offer; recording follows the same steps after a price is set.

faqs.q: Do I still record in Lawrenceburg for a house outside the city?
faqs.a: Yes. Anderson County has one clerk, and KRS 382.110 sends a deed to the clerk of the county holding the land, so a rural parcel goes to the same S Main Street office.

faqs.q: What does the clerk charge at minimum for a deed?
faqs.a: Fifty dollars, with $3 added for each page after the fifth. KRS 142.010 also lays a $4 state tax on conveyances, so ask for the full total first.

faqs.q: Is the seller or the buyer responsible for the transfer tax?
faqs.a: The seller, named as grantor, pays it. KRS 142.050 sets it at half a dollar per $500 of declared value, and the clerk collects it at the counter.
In the office, yes: the clerk says records and indexes are free to view there. Online viewing through eCCLIX costs money.
No. KRS 142.050 exempts foreclosure transfers and voluntary surrenders under a mortgage. The lender then has 45 days from signing to file that deed with the clerk, per KRS 382.110.
